In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the redox properties of bent metallocene dichloride complexes are determined by a balance between ligand field and ligand-to-ligand charge transfer interactions.
the redox and photophysical properties of bent metallocenes are governed by the identity of the group 4 transition metal, and by the ancillary π- (Cl, C5H5) and monodentatate σ- (Me, Cl) ligands.
the optical and electrochemical data can be combined for the purpose of determining the energy gap in the bent metallocene π-systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optical transitions in bent metallocene systems can be correlated to the redox potentials of the same molecules.

the optical and electrochemical properties of the metallocene complexes are strongly correlated and can be rationalised in terms of the molecular orbital theory and molecular electrostatic potential (MESP) maps.
the redox potentials of the metallocene dichloride complexes of the group 4 metals can be used to predict the energy of their lowest energy optical transitions, and vice versa.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the redox potentials of bent metallocene dichloride and dimethyl complexes are determined by the energy gap in the ground state of the complex.
redox potentials can be reliably estimated from the energies of optical L-to-M CT transitions.
the energy gap between the HOMO-to-HOMO and LUMO-to-LUMOMO redox transitions is a reliable diagnostic to determine relative energies of the HOMO and LMO in solution.
